title: Nanopore Long-Read Metabarcoding for Parasitic Nematodes Characterization
author: Lucas Huggins
materials: For the first step PCR amplification, two separate PCRs were conducted, one targeting the 18S rDNA of nematode clades I and IV and another targeting the ITS regions of the clade III and V nematodes. Both reactions were 25 µl PCRs conducted using 12.5 µl of LongAmp® Hot Start Taq 2× Master Mix (New England Biolabs, Massachusetts, USA) 8.5 µl Ambion nuclease-free water (Life Technologies, California, USA) herein referred to as water, 1 µl of forward primer, 1 µl of reverse primer and 2 µl of genomic faecal extracted DNA. The primers required include the addition of ONT adapter sequences that permit the addition of ONT indexes in a subsequent secondary PCR reaction. Hence, the primers for the 18S rDNA reaction were Nemabio18S-F_ONT : 5’-TTTCTGTTGGTGCTGATATTGCCGGTAGCAGTAACCGCCC -3’ and Nemabio18S-R_ONT: 5’-ACTTGCCTGTCGCTCTATCTTCATCATAATGATCTCTCCGCAGGTTCCACTCAC -3’, whilst for the ITS region reaction they were NemabioITS-F_ONT: 5’-TTTCTGTTGGTGCTGATATTGCCGTAGGTGAACTCGGGGAAGGATCATT -3’ and NemabioITS-R_ONT: 5’-ACTTGCCTGTCGCTCTATCTTCGCGGTAATACGAGCTGAGC -3’. PCRs were then conducted on a T100™ Thermal Cycler (Bio-Rad, California, USA) using the following conditions for the 18S rDNA reaction: 1 cycle of 94 °C for 1 min, 24 cycles of 94 °C for 30 s, 58 °C for 30 s and 65 °C for 45 s, with a final extension of 65 °C for 10 min. For the ITS region reaction conditions were: 1 cycle of 94 °C for 1 min, 25 cycles of 94 °C for 30 s, 58 °C for 30 s and 65 °C for 55 s, with a final extension of 65 °C for 10 min. The post-PCR 25 µl product of the ITS region reaction was then added to the product from the 18S rDNA reaction to create a total reaction output of 50 µl that was taken forward for further processing.

PCR product was then added to a 96-well plate and cleaned using a 1× ratio of NucleoMag NGS Clean-up and Size Select Beads (Macherey-Nagel, Duren, Germany) with a 15 min incubation on a HulaMixer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and two washes with freshly made 75% ethanol, followed by a final elution in 27 µl of water. Next, second step PCRs were conducted to add ONT barcodes to each samples’ amplicon and thereby permit multiplexing of up to 96 samples onto a flow cell. These secondary PCRs were 50 µl reactions utilising 25 µl of LongAmp® Taq 2× Master Mix (New England Biolabs), 24 µl of cleaned PCR product from the first PCR reaction and 1 µl of a unique barcode from the ONT PCR Barcoding Expansion 1-96 kit. Thermocycling conditions for this second reaction were 1 cycle of 95 °C for 3 min, 12 cycles of 95 °C for 15 s, 62 °C for 15 s and 65 °C for 1 min 5 s, with a final extension of 65 °C for 5 min. Secondary PCRs were followed by another clean-up step using a 0.55× ratio of NucleoMag beads to exclude and remove low molecular weight (smaller than 450 bp) PCR products, hence 27.5 µl of beads were used to clean 50 µl of PCR product with the same incubation and ethanol wash steps used as previously described and elution in 25 µl of water.

After rehydration the samples were spun down, water removed, and the faecal sample homogenised. Next 200 mg of homogenate was transferred to a bead-beating tube for DNA extraction using a QIAamp PowerFecal Pro DNA Kit (Qiagen, Hilden, Germany). Extraction was performed as per the manufacturer’s instructions with the addition of a minor modification incorporating an extra bead-beating step by adding 800 µl of CD1 buffer to the bead-beating tube in a FastPrep24 5G instrument (MP Biomedicals, California, USA). The final elution was conducted in 100 µL of elution buffer and stored at −20°C. Extractions can also be conducted using a different DNA extraction kit appropriate for removing faecal PCR inhibitors.
All DNA extracts were quantified using a Qubit™ 4 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Massachusetts, USA) using the dsDNA HS assay kit.

steps.title: Sample Rehydration
steps.instruction: Remove preservatives (e.g., 70% ethanol, 5% w/v potassium dichromate, or RNAlater) from faecal samples and add Milli-Q water to rehydrate for a minimum of 1 hour.

steps.title: PCR Barcoding and Amplification
steps.instruction: Perform library preparation using the PCR Barcoding Expansion 1-96 (EXP-PBC096) and ONT® Ligation Sequencing Kit (SQK-LSK114) following protocol ‘Ligation sequencing amplicons - PCR barcoding (SQK-LSK114 with EXP-PBC096)’ version PBBC9182v114rev107Mar2023.

substeps.instruction: Utilize separate physical laboratory areas for DNA extraction, pre-PCR, and post-PCR experiments.
Prepare all first-step PCRs in a PCR hood under sterile conditions using filter tips after UV sterilizing the workspace.
Include no-template PCR negative controls (water).
Include sequencing-run positive controls: gBlock synthetic DNA constructs of M. kandleri (793 bp) for 18S rDNA and A. fischeri (945 bp) for ITS region at a concentration of ~1 × 10^6 ng/µl.

steps.title: Amplicon Quality Control and Pooling
steps.instruction: Assess the amplification of a subset of samples and pool the barcoded products.

substeps.instruction: Verify product amplification using a 4200 TapeStation System and analyze DNA concentrations using a Qubit™ 4 Fluorometer.
Pool 4 µl of each barcoded and cleaned PCR product.
Concentrate the pool using a 2.5× ratio of NucleoMag beads.
Wash beads twice with 75% ethanol and elute in 50 µl of water.
Quantify the final pool on a Qubit™ 4 Fluorometer to ensure a minimum of 1,000 ng of DNA.

steps.title: Final Library Preparation
steps.instruction: Complete the library preparation using the NEBNext® Companion Module and SQK-LSK114 kit.

substeps.instruction: Perform DNA repair, end-prep, adapter ligation, and clean-up as per the ONT® protocol.
Dilute the final sequencing library to 50 fmol (assuming an average product fragment size of 1,400 bp).
Prime and load the R10.4-1 flow cells.

steps.title: Nanopore Sequencing
steps.instruction: Sequence the library on a MinION Mk1B or PromethION 2 (P2) solo device using MinKNOW version 24.02.8.

substeps.instruction: If re-using flow cells, treat with DNAse using the EXP-WSH004 Flow Cell Wash Kit (though not recommended).
Run fast base-calling for 22 - 47 hours.
Target an average per-sample sequencing depth of ~230,000 reads passing quality filtering (Q-score ≥ 8).

steps.title: Base-calling and Demultiplexing
steps.instruction: Process the raw sequencing data to obtain clean reads.

substeps.instruction: Demultiplex data using MinKNOW and concatenate fastq files for each barcode.
Base-call POD5 reads using the super accuracy model with Dorado version 7.3.11, removing barcodes, flanking sequences, and primer sequences.
Verify run success via MinKNOW by checking read size and pore activity.

steps.title: Sequence Separation and Binning
steps.instruction: Separate pooled 18S rDNA and ITS region sequences using pblat and seqtk.

substeps.instruction: Compare barcode data against a bespoke nematode 18S rDNA database using a pblat minimum score value of 50.
Extract matching sequences into an 18S rDNA file and assign remaining sequences to an ITS region file.

steps.title: Bioinformatic Processing with NanoCLUST
steps.instruction: Generate consensus sequences using the NanoCLUST pipeline and classify them against bespoke databases.

substeps.instruction: Apply 18S rDNA parameters: min length 600 bp, max length 1,200 bp, min cluster size 30, HDBSCAN epsilon 1, polish with 100 reads, 300,000 reads for UMAP.
Apply ITS parameters: min length 600 bp, max length 1,800 bp, min cluster size 30, HDBSCAN epsilon 1, polish with 100 reads, 300,000 reads for UMAP.
Classify sequences using blastn against bespoke 18S and ITS databases.
For sequences with identity scores <97%, further validate using blastn against the full GenBank database; remove sequences that cannot be correctly classified.

steps.title: Data Filtering and Thresholding
steps.instruction: Determine the final infection status by applying a read count cut-off threshold to eliminate false positives.

substeps.instruction: Identify the highest read-count of the M. kandleri or A. fischeri positive control sequences found in any non-positive control sample.
Set this maximum read-count as the batch threshold.
Define samples as negative if parasitic nematode reads are lower than this threshold.
